extracted.intended_audience: public company registrants preparing SEC filings and their accountants, auditors, and legal advisors
extracted.subtask_description: Interpretation and explanatory guidance for Rule 14-02 (Regulation S-X) and related Regulation S-K amendments requiring disclosure of climate-related severe weather events, other natural conditions, expenditures, recoveries, and impacts on financial estimates and assumptions in SEC filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate disclosure thresholds for balance sheet and income statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the final rules it is possible that the disclosure threshold could be triggered for a registrant's balance sheet, but not its income statement, and vice versa, resulting in only partial disclosure of capitalized costs, expenditures expensed, charges, and losses related to severe weather events and other natural conditions incurred during the fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that partial disclosure may occur; registrants may nonetheless disclose how the severe weather event or other natural condition affected both the income statement and balance sheet even if the disclosure threshold for one financial statement is not triggered (see discussion and 17 CFR 210.14-02).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of aggregate recoveries recognized
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules require a registrant to disclose the aggregate amount of any recoveries recognized during the fiscal year as a result of the severe weather events and other natural conditions for which capitalized costs, expenditures expensed, charges, or losses have been disclosed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 17 CFR 210.14-02(f). The Commission acknowledges that this may in some cases create the impression recoveries exceed expenditures, but registrants may provide additional explanatory disclosure about income statement and balance sheet effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: ’Severe’ modifies both weather events and other natural conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: For the avoidance of doubt, the agency is confirming that 'severe' modifies both the weather events and other natural conditions referenced in the rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 17 CFR 210.14-02(c),(d), and (h). This clarification is intended to eliminate confusion about the scope of covered events/conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enumerated examples of acute and chronic risks
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed and final amendments provide examples: Regulation S-K included hurricanes, floods, tornadoes, wildfires as examples of 'acute risks' and sustained higher temperatures, sea level rise, and drought as examples of 'chronic risks.' Final amendments to Regulation S-X include flooding, drought, wildfires, extreme temperatures, sea level rise, and add hurricanes and tornadoes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rules retain 'extreme temperatures' terminology in S-X instead of 'sustained higher temperatures' to emphasize disclosure is required only if the weather event or natural condition is 'severe'. Providing examples aids comparability and assists issuers in making disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: No requirement to determine cause of event
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants will not be required to determine the cause of the severe weather event or natural condition for purposes of providing disclosure under Rule 14-02; the cause is irrelevant in determining whether disclosure is required under Rules 14-01 and 14-02.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This simplifies the analysis for registrants and focuses disclosure on material impacts rather than attributing causation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural conditions need not be climate-related
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'natural conditions' referenced in Rule 14-02 need not be climate-related, and therefore may include types of non-climate-related occurrences, such as earthquakes, if severe and depending on the registrant's particular facts and circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure of non-climate-related severe weather events and other natural conditions is consistent with other event-based disclosure and can elicit material information for investors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples improve comparability and assist issuers
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing examples of severe weather events and other natural conditions will aid in the comparability of the resulting disclosure while assisting issuers in making the disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Proposing Release, section II.F.2; use examples as interpretive aids but apply facts and circumstances to determine materiality and severity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors for determining temperature-related severity
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining whether high temperatures constitute a severe natural condition, a relevant factor may include average seasonal temperatures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess local/seasonal baselines and compare current conditions to those baselines when evaluating whether temperatures are 'severe' for disclosure purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure requirements for carbon offsets and RECs
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the final rules, a registrant is required to disclose capitalized costs, expenditures expensed, and losses related to carbon offsets and RECs regardless of the reason for the expenditure (assuming the disclosure threshold is met).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 17 CFR 210.14-02(e). Registrants are not prevented from disclosing additional information about other transactions involving their carbon offsets and RECs; disclosure should include contextual information as discussed elsewhere (see infra section II.K.6.a.iii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible additional disclosure about offsets/RECs
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules do not prevent registrants from disclosing additional information about other transactions involving their carbon offsets and RECs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the rule requires certain amounts be disclosed, registrants may provide further detail (e.g., intended utilization, quantification, procurement/retirement practices) to aid investor understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expenditure metrics — treatment of capitalization vs expense timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules do not require a registrant to disclose both the capitalization of expenditures and subsequent expense of expenditures in the same period. Rather, the final rules require the disclosure of expenditures expensed and losses 'as incurred.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: if a registrant purchases new machinery to replace machinery damaged by a severe weather event, the registrant would disclose the cost to purchase the new machinery (if threshold met) but would not be required to disclose the subsequent depreciation associated with the machinery in the same period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregation and application of expenditure metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed Expenditure Metrics would have required a registrant to separately aggregate the amount of expenditures expensed and the amount of capitalized costs to determine whether the applicable disclosure threshold was triggered; the final rules discuss aggregation and thresholds in relation to 17 CFR 210.14-02(c) and (d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calculate disclosure thresholds using financial information consistent with the consolidated financial statements included in the filing; follow rules in 210.14-02(c)/(d) when aggregating relevant amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-referencing between Regulation S-X and S-K (subpart 1500)
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules include similar requirements under subpart 1500 of Regulation S-K to disclose material impacts on financial estimates and assumptions as a direct result of disclosed actions under a transition plan or as a direct result of a disclosed target or goal or actions taken to make progress toward meeting the target or goal. When responding to these Regulation S-K provisions, a registrant may cross-reference from the disclosure provided under 17 CFR 210.14-02(h) to the extent such disclosure is responsive to these subpart 1500 provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use cross-references where appropriate to avoid duplication, provided the cross-referenced disclosure is responsive to both requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trigger for disclosure of impacts on estimates and assumptions (Rule 14-02(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the registrant's estimates and assumptions were not materially impacted by exposures to risks and uncertainties associated with, or known impacts from, severe weather events and other natural conditions, or any climate-related targets or transition plans disclosed by the registrant, then no disclosure is required under Rule 14-02(h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only disclose material impacts on financial estimates and assumptions; assess whether impacts are material in the context of the registrant's financial statements and disclosed plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply the same accounting principles as rest of consolidated statements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission requires a registrant to apply the same set of accounting principles that it is required to apply in the preparation of the rest of its consolidated financial statements included in the filing, whenever applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 17 CFR 210.4-01(a)(1)-(2); financial statements not prepared in accordance with GAAP will be presumed misleading or inaccurate unless otherwise provided. Apply U.S. GAAP, IFRS, or other comprehensive sets of accounting principles consistently and reconcile where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of judgment and critical accounting estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants are regularly required to exercise judgment when applying GAAP to prepare their financial statements; financial estimates and assumptions impacted by climate-related events and transition risks are critical accounting estimates when they involve significant estimation uncertainty and are reasonably likely to have a material impact on the registrant's financial condition or results of operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize existing GAAP disclosure obligations (e.g., ASC 606, ASC 820, ASC 842) to disclose significant judgments and assumptions; see 17 CFR 229.303(b)(3) for definition of critical accounting estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and consolidation for disclosure thresholds (avoid double-counting)
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules require registrants to calculate the financial statement disclosure using financial information that is consistent with the scope of the rest of its consolidated financial statements included in the filing, which should not result in any double-counting or duplication (i.e., not evaluated at parent and subsidiary separately).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure disclosure thresholds are applied on the same consolidated basis as the filed financial statements to avoid duplication; consider the scope used for audited/balanced statements under 17 CFR 210.3-01(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgement of diversity in accounting practice for regulatory credits
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondents indicated that the lack of guidance in GAAP for accounting for regulatory credits (such as carbon offsets and RECs) results in a significant diversity in practice; FASB and IASB have projects to explore accounting for regulatory credits and pollutant pricing mechanisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that practice may vary and that standard-setter projects (FASB research project; IASB third agenda consultation) are underway; provide transparent disclosure about accounting policy choices and judgments for regulatory credits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of hurricanes and tornadoes in Rule 14-02(h)
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules added hurricanes and tornadoes to the list of severe weather events and other natural conditions included in Rule 14-02(h) to be consistent with additions in Rule 14-02(c) and (d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing whether to disclose under 14-02(h), consider these enumerated event types among the examples of severe events/conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure triggers off both balance sheet and income statement
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules call for disclosure triggered off both the balance sheet and the income statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess both financial statements when applying disclosure thresholds; either statement's threshold being met may trigger disclosure obligations under the rules.
